source: TSTD project (TA 7305-CAM), "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំពោត" (Corn Cultivation Technical Manual), Section 4.b: Pests and control, May 2012
text:
The manual describes two corn pests and their control methods:

1) Cutworm (ដង្កូវកាត់ស្លឹក / Cut Worm): This pest damages leaves and cuts through the tender growing parts (soft young leaves). The larva is dark-colored, feeds/hides on the leaf during the day, and is more active cutting stems at night. Control: cut off and remove infested leaves, burning or burying them away from the field; ensure good field drainage; encourage natural enemies to reduce yellowish egg masses; and if needed spray a registered pesticide such as chlorantraniliprole, indoxacarb, cypermethrin, methomyl, or fipronil, following label instructions.

2) Asian corn borer (ដង្កូវសៀងចោះពោត / Asian Corn Borer): The larva is white/cream-colored and bores into the plant. It damages the growing point of the corn plant -- the whorl, leaf, and stem tissue around the growing tip. Control: cut off and remove damaged parts, burning or burying them away from the field; ensure good drainage; encourage natural enemies (egg-mass predators/parasitoids); and if needed spray a registered pesticide such as chlorantraniliprole, indoxacarb, cypermethrin, methomyl, or fipronil, following label instructions.
